title: Output of the scenario-episode agent: an episode's screenplay

scenes.description: In episode order. Two to four for a whole episode.

fonction.description: (French) What the scene accomplishes in the episode.

ambiance.description: (French) The visual frame HELD over the whole scene, in one sentence: time of day, weather, general light. Sole exception to « no light » in this screenplay: it is continuity, not staging.

plans.description: In reading order. Order is that of the array: no plan number.

description.description: (French) The plan's intent, precise and complete: where the characters who matter start (relative to fixed landmarks of the place), the beats in order with visible gestures, what changes during the plan, how it ends (its last beat), and why it exists; then the lines said (each `NAME : « exact text »` on its own line, in the dialogue language). Narrative, with no framing, sound or camera movement, light only when it changes in the plan, no reference to another plan, no « État en fin de plan » line.

liaison.description: How this plan links to the PREVIOUS one (its only link: the description refers to no other plan). suite: it takes up where the previous plan ends (same place, same moment or seconds later, same people where the previous plan's last beat left them; its render continues the previous one without a cut). coupe: a clean cut (another place, another moment, another point of view). The first plan of the episode is a coupe. When unsure: coupe.

dureeSecondes.description: Generation duration, whole seconds, from 4 to 10 (never less than 4). It follows the brief's rhythm and what the moment holds (see the rules); group close moments into a single plan. A dialogue plan: generous duration, breathing margin of at least 2 s, to adjust after the voice take.

inventions.description: (French) Everything that was not in the brief. To validate or throw out.

notes.description: (French) Risky plans, duration trade-offs, proposed cuts for a dialogue that is too long. Empty if nothing to report.
